time_scope: modern Campidanese data synthesized from Bolognesi 1998 and related descriptions
claim: Word-initial voiceless /p t ʧ k/ and voiced /b d ʤ g/ are stops in absolute-initial and post-consonantal positions; in intervocalic contexts the voiceless series alternates with voiced spirants [β ð ʒ ɣ], while the voiced series has a more restricted, context-dependent pattern.
normalized_environment: VOICELESS_STOP -> VOICED_SPIRANT in LENITION contexts; STOP preserved WORD_INITIAL_ABSOLUTE and POSTCONSONANTAL
exceptions_or_counterexamples: A simple surface V_V rule overpredicts: intervocalic contexts can yield both spirants and geminates, and voiced stops do not pattern identically with voiceless stops.

claim: [z] is not contrastive and does not occur in absolute word-initial position; intervocalic [z] is analyzed as the voiced output of /s/.
exceptions_or_counterexamples: Chabot treats this as evidence against positing contrastive /z/; the record therefore encodes an analysis tied to distribution, not an independent inventory adjudication.

time_scope: modern morphophonological data summarized by Chabot
claim: Final /-t/ (3SG) and /-s/ (plural) may be followed by an epenthetic copy vowel; in that derived intervocalic environment the consonants surface lenited as [ð] and [z], respectively.
normalized_environment: FINAL_MORPHEME consonant + COPY_VOWEL creates LENITION context
scope: 3SG /-t/ and plural /-s/ at word edge with paragogic/epenthetic vowel
exceptions_or_counterexamples: The copy vowel is optional ('may surface'), so the intervocalic lenited realization is not the sole surface outcome of these morphemes.

claim: Lenition has explicit segment-class and lexical exceptions: /ʃː, ʦː, dz, v, ɖː/ do not undergo it in otherwise appropriate contexts; voiced stops vary and include lexical items in which deletion never occurs; nasals /n m ɲ/ do not lenite in external sandhi.
formal_environment: TARGET in LENITION_CONTEXT, with listed segment exclusions
normalized_environment: LENITION blocked for {ʃː,ʦː,dz,v,ɖː}; NASALS blocked EXTERNAL_SANDHI; VOICED_STOP deletion lexically variable
exceptions_or_counterexamples: Voiced-stop behavior is explicitly variable rather than categorically blocked; some lexical items never delete.

claim: Word-internal /n/ may lenite/delete only after the main stress-bearing vowel, whereas nasals do not show the corresponding external-sandhi alternation.
normalized_environment: /n/ LENITION/DELETION only WORD_INTERNAL AFTER MAIN_STRESS; not EXTERNAL_SANDHI
exceptions_or_counterexamples: Chabot explicitly separates this stress-dependent N-deletion from the general LENITION process because there is no matching sandhi alternation.

time_scope: modern synchronic pattern; Bolognesi 1998:419 as synthesized by Chabot
claim: South-Western rhotic metathesis is synchronically active in vowel-initial disyllables of the shape VrCV, moving /r/ from coda position into a preceding branching onset (CVrCV → CrVCV).
formal_environment: CVrCV → CrVCV; target word = VrCV, disyllabic
exceptions_or_counterexamples: Chabot contrasts this synchronic pattern with two other rhotic-metathesis patterns treated as diachronic, so they are not collapsed into one productive rule.

claim: Rhotic metathesis suppresses the initial vowel of the article and conditions different following-stop outputs: voiceless stops lengthen, while voiced stops spirantize.
exceptions_or_counterexamples: The voiced and voiceless series have complementary surface effects rather than one uniform phonetic strengthening outcome.

time_scope: modern synchronic sandhi; historically conditioned lexical trigger set
claim: Certain unstressed vowel-final monosyllabic prepositions/connectives that historically lost a final consonant trigger raddoppiamento-like strengthening of a following initial consonant; the triggering property is lexically restricted.
normalized_environment: LEXICALLY_MARKED UNSTRESSED_MONOSYLLABLE -> FORTITION of FOLLOWING_WORD_INITIAL C
scope: external sandhi after specified function words
exceptions_or_counterexamples: Not every vowel-final word triggers the process; the trigger set is a lexical subset associated historically with lost codas. Southern Sardinian varieties may also differ in voiced-stop realization.
